metadata.title: Cape Cod Railroad (with Cape Cod Central, and the Old Colony / New Haven lines beyond it)
metadata.description: The Cape Cod Branch Railroad (renamed Cape Cod Railroad 1854) from Middleborough to Sandwich (1848), West Barnstable (1853) and Hyannis (1854) with the Hyannis Wharf boat-train spur; the Cape Cod Central's Yarmouth - Orleans (1865), bought 1868; and the Orleans - Wellfleet extension (1871). After the 1872 Old Colony merger, only the pieces no other layer draws are carried on: the Woods Hole Branch, Yarmouth - Provincetown and the Chatham Branch, each split Old Colony (1872-1893) / New Haven (1893-). Middleborough - Hyannis after 1872 is NOT drawn here (see not_yet_sourced).
not_yet_sourced: FOLLOW-UP (existing layer, not edited here): mbta_commuter_rail.geojson 'MBTA Commuter Rail: CapeFLYER' draws Middleborough - Hyannis 1848-1959 as the MBTA. Per the research report it overstates Sandwich - Hyannis by 1848-1853 (opened Dec 1853 / 1854), carries 111 years under the wrong company (Cape Cod RR 1848-1872, Old Colony 1872-1893, New Haven 1893-1959; MBTA from 1964 only), and has no geometry_quality noting the pre-1911 canal alignment. The fix is to split that segment (Old Colony 1872-1893 and New Haven 1893-1959 features for Middleborough - Hyannis, and Fall River RR / Old Colony eras north of Middleborough) - deliberately not done in this layer.

Cape Cod Central 1865-1868: whether it ran its own trains or was worked by the Cape Cod Railroad is not established; drawn under the Cape Cod Central (owner and builder). Best sources: Cape Cod RR annual reports 1866-68, Barnstable Patriot / Yarmouth Register 1865.
Old Colony merger effective date: 1 May (WOC) / 30 Sep (WCCR) / 1 Oct / 5 Oct 1872 (SET). Year firm; 1872 is shared by the Cape Cod RR and Old Colony segments.
Woods Hole Branch July-Sept 1872 operator: Cape Cod RR (WHHC/SET project) vs Old Colony (WOC). Drawn as Old Colony from 1872; no Cape Cod RR era drawn.
Through running Boston - Middleborough 1848-1872: whether Cape Cod RR trains ran north of Middleborough is not established; only its own track is drawn.
Wellfleet opening: 28 Dec 1870 (SET) vs January 1871 (FED); drawn from 1871. Harwich opening 5 vs 6 Oct 1865 (year firm). West Barnstable 22 Dec vs ~Thanksgiving 1853 (year firm).
[OPEN] start: Hyannis - Hyannis Wharf, first confirmed 1866 (bracket 1854-1866).
[OPEN] end: New Haven Yarmouth - Provincetown, last confirmed 1932 (WCCC's uncited 1938 not used).
[OPEN] both ends: New Haven Chatham Branch, confirmed 1894-1920 only; 1887-1893 operator unchecked (held).
Woods Hole summer trains 1960-1964 and New York - Hyannis summer trains 1960/61-1964: route/years not sourced, not drawn.
FED says the 1861 Woods Hole charter was renamed 'Cape Cod Central Railroad' in 1864, conflicting with WCCR (Vineyard Sound RR -> Plymouth and Vineyard Sound RR). Recorded, not resolved.
All headways and speeds are estimates.
branches_deliberately_omitted: Old Colony / New Haven Middleborough - Hyannis 1872-1959 (report block [10]): already drawn, under the wrong company, by the MBTA CapeFLYER feature; correcting that is a separate follow-up (see not_yet_sourced), so no duplicate geometry is added here.
Sandwich - West Barnstable / Barnstable / Yarmouth interim termini of 1854 (block [2]): invisible on a year slider; folded into the West Barnstable - Hyannis feature from 1854.
Cape Cod Railroad era of the Woods Hole Branch (block [8]): drawable NONE - 1872 operator contested.
Hyannis Wharf after 1872 (block [12]): no passenger service after July 1872 (WHYA).
Freight afterlives (Outer Cape, Woods Hole, Hyannis line 1959/64-1984, Chatham): Rule 1. Later tourist operators (Cape Cod & Hyannis, Bay Colony, Cape Cod Central 1999-): out of this report's scope.
metadata.geometry_note: Traced with opstrace.py (Overpass mail.ru mirror + OpenHistoricalMap). Every grade on the Cape is tagged old_railway_operator=NYNH&H in OSM (live Mass Coastal/Cape Cod Central track, Cape Cod Rail Trail, Shining Sea Bikeway, Old Colony Rail Trail); OHM supplied the lifted Outer Cape, Chatham and Hyannis Wharf stretches. No straight-line legs anywhere. Pre-canal (pre-1911/1914) alignment at Buzzards Bay - Sagamore is not mapped in OSM or OHM, so the 1848-1911 years are drawn on the post-canal route (stated per feature).
metadata.freight_only_audit: No freight-only years drawn: every line ends at its passenger end or at a change of operator; freight afterlives are mentioned in notes only.
metadata.horsecar_audit: None: all lines were locomotive-worked from opening (the horse-drawn element in the record is the Yarmouth - Orleans stagecoach the railroad replaced).

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap (CC0, geometry only - its dates are not used), traced with opstrace.py over ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYNH&H, untagged rail and rail-trails; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg. Drawn 27.8 mi against 27.6 mi documented (WCCR: 14.7 Middleborough - Wareham + 12.9 to Sandwich; Fowler line 92: 34.6 - 62.5 = 27.9). Composition: 26.1 mi OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYNH&H (live Mass Coastal / Cape Cod Central track and rail-trails); 1.7 mi untagged OSM railway ways. Every waypoint station lies within 0.6 km of the drawn line; no out-and-back spurs. Starts at the old Middleborough depot and follows the present track south to the Cape Main Subdivision. ERA ALIGNMENT (Rule 2): this feature's years predate the 1909-1914 Cape Cod Canal, which relocated the line. The pre-canal route Buzzards Bay - Monument (Bourne 1st) - North Sandwich (Bournedale 1st) - Sagamore ran through the Monument River / Scusset valley that the canal now occupies (Fowler line 92: 'Former route until 1911'); neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap maps it (OHM has only a ~0.6 mi pre-1914 piece at the Buzzards Bay crossing, which coincides with the drawn track within about 5 m). So Buzzards Bay - Sagamore (about 6 mi) is DRAWN ON THE POST-CANAL ALIGNMENT along the canal's south bank, a later alignment than this era; displacement is a few hundred metres to about 1 km.

segments.note: Built and run by the Cape Cod Branch Railroad (chartered 1846), renamed the Cape Cod Railroad on 22 Feb 1854 - a rename of the same company, so one feature and one colour. Middleborough (junction with the Fall River Railroad) - Wareham opened 26 Jan 1848, through to Sandwich 26 May 1848 (WCCR, SET; WSAN 'May 1848'; New-York Daily Tribune 27 May 1848: 'has been opened'). Fowler's 1850 Pathfinder letters show every intermediate stop served and Sandwich as the terminus. Sandwich was the end of the line until the extension of Dec 1853 (drawn as a separate feature). Whether Cape Cod trains ran through to Boston over the Fall River RR / Old Colony is not established, so only the company's own track (Middleborough and south) is drawn. The Cape Cod Railroad merged into the Old Colony in 1872; the year is firm but the effective date conflicts (1 May per WOC, 30 Sep per WCCR, 5 Oct per SET), so 1872 is shared with the Old Colony era. After 1872 this corridor carried passengers under the Old Colony and the New Haven (to 1959); those eras are not drawn here (see metadata). Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: opening dates from WCCR, SET, WSAN and two in-era newspapers (New-York Daily Tribune 27 May 1848, New York Herald 21 May 1848); 1850 service at every stop from Fowler line 92 letter x; merger year from WOC, WCCR, SET. Headway not sourced.

The Cape Cod Railroad merged into the Old Colony in 1872; the year is firm but the effective date conflicts (1 May per WOC, 30 Sep per WCCR, 5 Oct per SET), so 1872 is shared with the Old Colony era. segments.note: Boat-train extension to the Nantucket steamers. START IS [OPEN]: 1866 is the earliest CONFIRMED year (Fowler line 97, 'Hyannis Wharf p2' = 1866 Pathfinder), not the opening. The wharf spur was a condition of Nantucket subscriptions and the steamer ran from Sept 1854 (WCCR, SET), but no source dates the first passenger train onto the wharf, so the start is bracketed 1854-1866 and held at 1866. Do not move it earlier without evidence. END is firm: passenger service between Hyannis and the wharf ended in July 1872 when the Woods Hole branch opened and the island boats moved there (WHYA); no passenger trains ran to the wharf after 1872. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1866 service from Fowler line 97 letter p2; July 1872 end from WHYA; WCCR and SET for the steamer context only (they do not date the first train). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Opened by the Cape Cod Central Railroad (incorporated 1861): to Harwich in October 1865 (Springfield Weekly Republican 30 Sep 1865, 'to be opened to Harwich October 6'; SET gives 5 Oct) and to Orleans in December 1865 (WCCC; SET 6 Dec 1865; Worcester Daily Spy 12 Dec 1865: 'opened to public travel last week. The coaches on the Yarmouth and Orleans route have made their last trip'). Bought by the Cape Cod Railroad 21 Apr 1868 (WOC; SET 'May 1868'), consolidated 28 Jul 1868. OPERATOR LABEL IS OPEN: no source checked says whether the Cape Cod Central ran its own trains or was worked by the Cape Cod Railroad from opening (WCCC/WOC call it 'a branch of the Cape Cod Railroad'); it is drawn under the company that owned and opened it. If it proves to have been worked by the Cape Cod Railroad, recolour these years to the Cape Cod Railroad. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: opening from three in-era newspapers (SWR65, WDS65, SWR66) and WCCC, SET; purchase/consolidation from WOC and SET. Operator not established; headway not sourced.

segments.note: Extension to Wellfleet. Opening in CONFLICT: 28 Dec 1870 (SET, uncited blog: 'First passenger train arrived in Wellfleet December 28, 1870') vs January 1871 (FED); WWEL and WHS say only 1870. Drawn from 1871, the later and confirmed year; the bracket is 1870-1871. Wellfleet was the terminus until the Old Colony reached Provincetown in 1873. The Cape Cod Railroad merged into the Old Colony in 1872; the year is firm but the effective date conflicts (1 May per WOC, 30 Sep per WCCR, 5 Oct per SET), so 1872 is shared with the Old Colony era. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

Every waypoint station lies within 0.6 km of the drawn line; no out-and-back spurs. Buzzards Bay - Falmouth on the live Falmouth Line (Mass Coastal), Falmouth - Woods Hole on the Shining Sea Bikeway, both tagged NYNH&H. ERA ALIGNMENT (Rule 2): the branch leaves the main line at Buzzards Bay and is drawn over the post-canal crossing (the canal opened 1914; the present lift bridge dates from 1935). For 1872-1914 the first ~0.5 mi at Buzzards Bay is a later alignment than the era drawn: OpenHistoricalMap's short 1854-1914 main-line piece there coincides with today's track, but the pre-canal junction layout is not mapped.

segments.note: Cohasset Narrows (Buzzards Bay) - Woods Hole, opened July 1872 (17 Jul WCCR, 18 Jul WHHC/FED/SET, 20 Jul WOC table - day in conflict, year firm). It was planned and begun by the Cape Cod Railroad (announced 8 Sep 1871, ground broken 11/12 Sep 1871; WHHC, SET), but the Old Colony merger fell in 1872 and whether a Cape Cod Railroad train ever ran on the branch is unsettled (WOC: merger effective 1 May, branch 'built by the Old Colony'; WCCR: 'completed after the merger'). So no Cape Cod Railroad era is drawn and the branch starts under the Old Colony, which certainly ran it within months. Island steamers moved here from Hyannis. Old Colony leased to the New Haven 1 Mar 1893. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: opening from WCCR, WHHC, FED, SET, WOC (day conflict recorded); 1876 service from Fowler line 96 letter y at Falmouth; 1893 lease from WOC. Headway not sourced.

Lifted: about half on OSM grade tagged NYNH&H (Old Colony Rail Trail and abandoned ways), the rest on OpenHistoricalMap's Chatham branch.

segments.note: Harwich - Chatham, built by the separate Chatham Railroad Company and opened 21 Nov 1887 (WOC table; WCCC). BOTH ENDS ARE [OPEN]. Who ran it 1887-1893 (an Old Colony lease is assumed by most accounts) was not checked, so 1887-1893 is held, not drawn. 1894 is the first CONFIRMED year of New Haven-era service (Fowler line 98 letter z = 1894 Pathfinder / 1893-96 New Haven timetables) and 1920 the last (letter b); Chatham has no 1932 letter, but absence is not evidence of an end. The New Haven acquired the Chatham Railroad in 1905 (WOC table). Do not extend either end without evidence. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the drawn years rest only on Fowler's timetable letters (z, a, b = 1894, 1904, 1920); the 1887 opening and 1905 acquisition are from the WOC table. Headway not sourced.
